card.title: AC voltage applied to resistor, inductor, and capacitor

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A resistor takes an in-phase current and dissipates I_rms squared R. An inductor has reactance 2πfL and makes the voltage lead. A capacitor has reactance 1/(2πfC) and makes the current lead. Pure L and C exchange energy with the source and take no average power.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
C = Q/V
C = ε₀A/d
U = ½CV²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Take π = 3.14 when a decimal reactance is required.  ·  A lamp in series with a coil is dimmer on AC than the resistance alone would suggest.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: When a sinusoidal voltage is applied to a pure resistor, the current follows the voltage with no delay. The rms current is the rms voltage divided by R, and the average power is the heating I_rms squared times R.  ·  A pure inductor opposes a changing current. Its reactance is X_L = 2πfL, so a higher frequency or a larger inductance means a smaller current. The voltage leads the current by a quarter of a cycle, and the average power is zero.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: ac voltage applied to resistor, inductor, capacitor (within Alternating Current).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Physics — don't mix them.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Resistive AC  ·  Inductive reactance  ·  Capacitive reactance  ·  rms values

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Resistor: current and voltage in phase.  ·  Inductor: current lags by 90°.  ·  Capacitor: current leads by 90°.  ·  Use rms with rms.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Capacitance C = Q/V; parallel-plate C = ε₀A/d (larger with dielectric: C = ε₀εᵣA/d).  ·  Energy stored U = ½CV² = Q²/2C.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Why is the average power zero in a pure inductor?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A 50 Hz supply of 10 V rms is connected to a 0.20 H pure inductor. Find X_L. Take π = 3.14.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: In a pure resistor the phase difference is → B  ·  X_L increases when → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: A pure capacitor opposes a change of voltage. Its reactance is X_C = 1/(2πfC), which is large at low frequency and small at high frequency. The current leads the voltage by a quarter cycle, and again the average power is zero.  ·  The three elements are drawn as phasors. The resistor voltage lies along the current. The inductor voltage is drawn 90° ahead of the current. The capacitor voltage is drawn 90° behind the current.  ·  Household meters read rms values. A peak of 10√2 volts has an rms value of 10 V. Mixing a peak voltage with an rms current gives a wrong power.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ capacitance c = q/v; parallel-plate c = ε₀a/d (larger with dielectric: c = ε₀εᵣa/d)..  ·  The resistor does not shift the phase.  ·  X_L rises with frequency and X_C falls.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Average power in a pure L or C is zero.  ·  rms is the peak divided by √2, not by 2.  ·  Name the element before the phase.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Keep peak and rms in separate lines of the working.  ·  Write I_rms = V_rms / R and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.  ·  Series: 1/C = Σ1/C (same Q); Parallel: C = ΣC (same V).  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Limit to remember: capacitance c = q/v; parallel-plate c = ε₀a/d (larger with dielectric: c = ε₀εᵣa/d).  ·  A real coil is an inductor with resistance in series.
